title: cross-environment stream + toolcall golden/regression suite and CI canary
creator: Diego Ramirez
description: Create a cross-environment golden prompt and contract regression suite that validates streaming API semantics, function/tool-calling interleavings, and structured-output resilience across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to detect regressions in: (1) streaming chunk boundaries and event ordering, (2) tool/function call serialization and tool invocation handoff, (3) partial/ndjson structured output recovery, and (4) fallback behavior when model variants or quantized kernels are used. This ticket scopes the test artifacts, CI pipelines, canonical seeds, and a canary runner that executes on each merge to main and nightly on Dedicated/private staging clusters.
acceptance_criteria: A golden prompt corpus (>= 120 prompts) covering short/long sequences, interleaved tool calls, partial JSON, and backpressure scenarios is checked into tests/api/golden-corpus with metadata for expected event sequences.
Contract assertions implemented for: chunk ordering, toolcall start/complete events, tool ID/idempotency, correct schema recovery for partial JSON + schema fallback, and KV-cache priming visibility.
CI pipeline jobs (gha) added: smoke-canary (fast, per-PR), nightly-full (longer, cross-model), and staging-canary (runs against Dedicated staging infra). Failures block merge for P0 regressions.
A lightweight simulator/stub for tools (python/ts) that can be used in local runs and CI to deterministically reproduce toolcall interleavings is included and documented.
Dashboards in Grafana for canary runs with pass/fail, latency histograms for streaming chunks, and delta diffs for structured-output fp32->quantized variants are available.
Docs describing how to add new golden prompts, how to write contract assertions, and how to run the suite locally are published in Confluence and linked from the ticket.
subtasks: Design golden prompt taxonomy and tagging scheme (owner: Lena) - include edgecases: nested toolcalls, aborted toolcall, payload truncation
Implement deterministic tool stub harness (owner: Raj Patel) - python + node stubs with configurable delay and jitter
Author contract assertion library (owner: Mei Chen) - streaming-order, idempotency, schema-fallback matchers
Integrate suite into PR smoke-canary GH action (owner: SRE team) - fast path uses small subset and mocked runtime
Add staging-canary job to Jenkins/Dedicated CI that runs against dedicated-staging cluster (owner: Infra Ops)
Create Grafana dashboard and alerting for nightly regressions (owner: Observability)
decisions: Use NDJSON framing for structured-output golden expectations to avoid brittle chunk boundaries; contract assertions operate on reassembled logical messages rather than raw byte chunks.
Golden seeds will be tied to a fingerprint file (sha256) per model variant; CI will flag mismatches and create an auto-issue template for investigation.
Tool stubs are deterministic and use a scripted timeline to reproduce race conditions; real tool integrations are tested separately in a smaller integration matrix.
Prefer fast PR smoke-canary against mocked runtime to keep developer iteration time low; escalate failing smoke runs to staging-canary against real infra for debugging.
progress_updates: 2025-02-03: Kickoff meeting with Eng/PM/QA. Agreed golden corpus size target and CI gates. Assigned owners for tool harness and assertion lib.
2025-02-06: Draft taxonomy (short/long, nested-tools, aborted, partial-json, backpressure) reviewed by PM + Observability. Minor edits requested to include quantized-model scenarios.
2025-02-09: Initial tool stub prototype landed in repo test-harness/tool-stub with deterministic timeline; basic interleaving repro works locally (PR #5123).

2025-02-12: Contract assertion prototype for chunk ordering and toolcall idempotency implemented. Running end-to-end smoke locally against mock runtime; found a race in toolcall-complete event ordering—opened ENG-11828 to track fix.
2025-02-14: CI smoke-gha job drafted and running on feature branch; two flaky tests identified related to simulated jitter—SRE assigned to stabilize runner.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Kumar): Ensure docs include how to add narrowly-scoped golden prompts for customer-reported regressions; prefer small, focused seeds for rapid triage.
Design (Omar Li): Request sample visual flowchart in Confluence showing streaming chunk lifecycle and where assertions attach (start, mid, complete).
SRE (Maya Singh): Recommend containerizing the tool stub to reduce environment drift in CI and to allow reuse in Dedicated staging runs.
Security (Priya Nair): Note that tool stubs should not store customer payloads in plaintext during test runs in staging; use ephemeral logs and redaction.
notes: Trade-off: prioritizing reassembled logical message assertions reduces false positives but may mask subtle chunk-level regressions; plan to keep a small set of raw-chunk assertions for critical paths.
Backpressure scenarios will be simulated by varying write buffer sizes + artificial delays in the stub; ensure tests cover both small and large token outputs.
We will version golden corpus metadata so teams can opt-in to strict vs permissive assertion modes during rollouts.
how_to_run_local: Checkout repo and run `make test-golden` (requires docker).
To run full suite (long): `pytest tests/golden --tag nightly --max-runtime 7200`
